age_experience_notes: Age limits at enrolment: younger than 21 for first-level studies (undergraduate academic, integrated academic, undergraduate vocational); younger than 25 for first-level specialist vocational studies and for second-level studies (master's academic, master's vocational, specialist academic); younger than 35 for doctoral academic studies. No work experience is required.
programmes_note: Study is in Serbian, with the possibility of consultations in English at the university. Holders first take an intensive Serbian course and enrol in a programme of their choice in the following academic year (2027/2028), after passing a Serbian language exam and the entrance exam of the chosen faculty. The scholarship covers one level of study and one programme in it; a change of programme is not allowed. The Ministry publishes a list of institutions and, for master's studies after a three-year bachelor's, a short list of named programmes. The scholarship pages do not give a field-by-field catalogue; the list is of faculties, not courses.
institutions_note: State higher education institutions founded by the Republic of Serbia: the University of Belgrade, the University of Novi Sad, the University of Kragujevac and the University of Nis, plus academies and colleges of applied studies. The ministry list also names the University of Art in Belgrade, the State University of Novi Pazar (heading only), the vocational academies and the colleges in Vojvodina. The applicant chooses a faculty and sits its entrance exam in June; a candidate who cannot get a place may sit entrance exams at state institutions in later admission periods where places remain. Housing is in state student centres in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Nis and Kragujevac.

summary.detail: First-level studies: undergraduate academic, integrated academic or undergraduate vocational studies. Entry: completed four-year secondary education; younger than 21. Study programmes are in Serbian after the preparatory Serbian course; the Serbian language exam and the faculty entrance exam must be passed before enrolment. Free tuition covers one level of studies.

summary.detail: Second-level studies: master's academic, master's vocational and specialist academic studies; candidate must be younger than 25. A 60-ECTS master's needs a relevant bachelor's with at least 240 ECTS or a relevant four-year degree; a 120-ECTS master's needs a relevant bachelor's with at least 180 ECTS. The programme page adds that a vocational master's needs a relevant undergraduate or specialist vocational diploma, or an undergraduate academic one, with at least 180 ECTS. The same institutions as for bachelor's are listed; for master's after a three-year bachelor's the ministry names the programmes below (University of Belgrade).

summary.detail: Third-level doctoral academic studies; candidate must be younger than 35. Entry: finished undergraduate and master's academic studies (or integrated studies) with an overall pass grade of 80 percent. The programme page gives a different threshold (average grade at least 8.5, and integrated studies of at least five years and 300 ECTS). Documents include a certificate of the average grade of the previous level. Doctoral scholarship holders must also pass the year's exams, show approval of research topics and seminars, and show registration or approval of the dissertation topic; the scholarship ends if the dissertation is not defended within the legal time. No doctoral programmes are named; the institution list covers doctoral academic studies for candidates with a master's diploma.

summary.detail: First-level specialist vocational studies (and vocational courses in general) are covered; candidate must be younger than 25. Health documentation signed and stamped by a doctor at a recognised health institution in the home country, diagnoses in Latin with ICD codes: (1) vaccination record showing tuberculosis, hepatitis B, polio, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, measles, mumps, rubella, Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae; (2) medical certificate on general health, chronic conditions, current treatment and a psychological or psychiatric assessment; (3) lab results for HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, tuberculosis (QuantiFERON-TB or chest X-ray) and malaria. Completed and signed application form (filled in online), with copies of the documents and the health certificate given to the competent institution of the home country for endorsement

application_steps.title: Fill in the online form and email scanned documents
application_steps.detail: Complete the online application form and email the scanned original documents, with translations into Serbian or English certified by an authorised person, to the Ministry's project mailbox. The call notice gives the application window as 18 May to 1 June 2026. Documents not translated into English or Serbian are not considered.

application_steps.title: Get your country's endorsement
application_steps.detail: Give a copy of the documents, the signed form and the health certificate with test results to the competent institution in your country for formal endorsement. That institution sends its list of endorsed candidates to the Serbian embassy or consulate. The mission may also propose a candidate who is not on the list.

application_steps.title: Review by an inter-ministerial commission
application_steps.detail: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs sends the nominee lists and application forms to the Ministry of Education by 10 June. A commission of the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Agency for Qualifications (ENIC/NARIC) and the Student Health Care Institute of Belgrade reviews the files. The Minister decides the final list by 26 June, and embassies are told between 27 June and 4 July. Each participating state must nominate endorsed candidates. The Ministry may reject an application if the health documents cannot be verified or the health state is incompatible with shared accommodation.

application_steps.title: Sign the contract and arrive in Belgrade
application_steps.detail: A scholarship contract is signed with the Ministry of Education. Arrive in Belgrade between 15 October and 15 November, bring the original documents (translated) and the original health documents, and take a mandatory medical examination at the Student Health Care Institute of Belgrade. Help is provided from airport reception onward.

application_steps.title: Learn Serbian, pass the entrance exam and enrol
application_steps.detail: Phase one is an intensive Serbian course until June, with preparatory lessons for admission. After the Serbian exam, sit the entrance exam of the chosen faculty in the June admission period and enrol for 2027/2028. Holders who already studied in Serbia skip the course and take the entrance exam for the next level. If no place is won, entrance exams can be taken in later admission periods where places remain.

application_steps.title: Keep the scholarship during studies and return home
application_steps.detail: Earn at least 37 ECTS credits each academic year to re-enrol as a funded student; an extra year after the final year is kept if every year met that mark. Keep your passport valid, regularise your residence on time, report changes in student status to the Ministry within 30 days, and return to the nominating country after the studies. A next level needs a new competition. The scholarship can end for false documents, failing the Serbian exam, failing the credit rule, not completing the cycle, or breaking the contract or rules.

fetch_problems: The English list of institutions is a scanned image PDF with no text layer; I read it page by page as images (list labelled 2024, on the 2026 call page).
notes: The deadline in the 2026 project description and call notice is 1 June 2026 (window 18 May to 1 June). The programme page still shows 26 June 2026 as the closing date and lists 10 June and 3 July for later steps; it looks like text from an earlier call, so the project description was followed.
Doctoral entry: the 2026 project description says overall pass grade of 80 percent; the programme page says average grade at least 8.5. The 2026 description was used first and both are noted.
The Serbian course start is given as September to June in one place and October 2026 to June 2027 elsewhere in the same description; holders arrive between 15 October and 15 November.

The list of institutions on the call page is labelled 2024; the ministry should confirm it is current. It names the University of Art in Belgrade and the State University of Novi Pazar, which the project description does not list by name.
